recipes.name: Pittsburgh Steelers Game Day Sampler
ingredients_raw: salt and cracked black pepper to taste

steps.text: Melt butter in a large, nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add onion; cook until very tender, about 10 minutes. Stir in as much cabbage as fits in the skillet; cook until cabbage is very tender, about 15 minutes. Stir in remaining cabbage as mixture cooks down.

Meanwhile, fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rapid boil. Cook egg noodles at a boil until tender yet firm to the bite, about 5 minutes. Drain well in a colander set in the sink.

Stir kielbasa into cabbage mixture; cook until warm, 3 to 5 minutes. Fold in egg noodles, then gently fold in pierogis. Cover skillet; cook until pierogis are hot in the center, about 10 minutes more. Season with salt and black pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Pittsburgh Steelers Game Day Sampler
raw_recipe.description: This Pittsburgh Steelers game day sampler recipe is a tasty tailgating favorites combo: buttery haluski, mini pierogis, and kielbasa all in one dish.

review.reviewBody: I’m from Cleveland, but I love this Cincinnati chili!
I add 1/2 lb of bacon then brown the kielbasa, add some chicken broth for moisture, then top it off with dill.

Loved this! I used a wok and kept things warm in the crockpot as I cooked them. I browned the kielbasa in butter, removed with slotted spoon then browned the pierogies in the remaining butter. Removed those then added more butter and sautéed the onions until soft. Once they were cooked I mixed in the cabbage and cooked about 15 minutes until tender. Like other reviewers I added about a cup of beef broth to the cabbage onion mixture. I also boiled the noodles in beef broth. It was very flavorful!

Really good! I knew this would make a lot so I cut it back to 1/2 bag of noodles, 1 box pierogies, and 1 LB cabbage with the smoked sausage. I didn't have a skillet big enough- so after frying the sliced smoked sausage, I combined that with the cooked noodles in a large crockpot. I then fried up the cabbage and onions in the sausage drippings-- gave the cabbage a nice flavor, added boiled pierogies until heated through. I combined everything in the crockpot & left it on keep warm until it was time to eat. My husband said it didn't look like it would be any good but then RAVED about it! Would be good to take to a potluck as written.

This was delicious!!! I used regular sized pierogis and boiled them according to package directions before adding them. I think sauteing the onions in bacon grease would add a good flavor and a little saltiness, which would be good. Even our picky kids liked this, and we will definitely add it to our regular rotation!
Definitely hits home now living in SW Florida. But changes where that I smokeked raw kielbasa with pecan wood and used Amidh made Kluski noodles. Came out amazing!

This meal rocks!!! I’m from PA but live in Texas now so I couldn’t find the Pierogies?. I did add thick cut bacon to it. I cooked it in the oven @400 for 8 min and then cut it up. I also used Slap Ya Momma seasoning in it. Also used Amish style noodles.
Love it. I cooked the noodles with some Beef bullion, and added broth to the cabbage as suggested. I can't wait until next seas on to cook it for my next steelers game at my house. Go Steelers!

If you need a delicious meal that feeds a lot, this is your recipe. I made this as written with the only addition being that I cooked the noodles in beef stock. I knew from the ingredients that this was going to make a very large amount. I decided to use the wok as it is very wide and I knew it would accommodate everything, it worked perfectly. While cooking I did add about ½ cup of the beef stock that I cooked the noodles in to give it a little more moisture while the meat and pierogies were browning. I served this with fresh diced tomatoes and sour cream. We loved it and I MOST definitely will be making this one again.

Easy to make, love one dish meals, but it was a little bland. I expected this so I added some freshly diced garlic, and a little bit of Lawrys. Like another reviewer I boiled my egg noodles in beef stock. Also, as I was eating it, it occurred to me that with the egg noodles and the pierogies (which I lightly browned first) it was a little too noodley. I think I'd like it better with some baby red potatoes instead of pierogies, and some more seasoning.

This was a quick meal for supper, this would be good on a winters day in a roaster pan for a tailgate party. I used ball park franks and andouille sausage, it's what i had on hand & worked great, I just grilled them first then added to my pot of noodles, cabbage, and small red potatoes that i par boiled first.

Made this for my residents at work with the gluten free pasta & they loved it. You can use any type of pasta: bow-ties, penne, shells, elbows, rotini, or wheat, gluten free, etc. Made for my family tonight & it was also a hit! Keep up the good work Allrecipes!!

This recipe made very large amount of food. Good flavor, the only thing I might change is adding more meat and cooking the pierogies prior to placing them with the rest of the food to get a crisp shell. Most certainly making this again.
Everyone loved it!
Added chicken broth to give more moisture and ability to stir. Needed a wider pot than I used. Piriogi

I substituted kale for cabbage, whole wheat pasta for noodles, hot links for kielbasa and meatballs for pierogis. Was limited by what they sell at Trader Joe’s. And then added sour cream, smoked Gouda and feta. Had some in the fridge. Probably made it a completely different recipe but it was sooooooooioo good.

I just made this. It was pretty good. It did lack flavor. Next time I will do as suggested by others, and cook the noodles in beef broth, add a little Worcestershire sauce and add some bacon. It makes a lot of food, I need a bigger pan!!

This is a stellar recipe! I didn't use perogies, but I definitely will next time. I've made this now every week and has been added into a weekly menu. This was a smash hit, family and friends loved it. Thank you for sharing this recipe!

My boyfriend is from Pittsburgh and die hard Steelers fan. I made this to surprise him, yet he, his family or friends (all from Pittsburgh) never heard of this recipe. We were not amazed with a big mush this was. It was edible but not something that's presentable.

This was a good, inexpensive, quick meal. My grocery store doesn't carry mini perogies so I had no choice but to omit them. It's a tad bit bland, but I added a few dashes of Worcestershire sauce and a clove of chopped garlic. Thanks for sharing!
